repairAudit.claim: the totality inversion was type-level while NT-3 and NT-5 tested content-level violations inside admitted types
repairAudit.measured: outputLaw.refusal.rule is rewritten to two limbs. Type-level: any provider output that is not an admitted semantic output type or an admitted existing protocol frame is refused before admission. Content-level: an output of an admitted type is admitted only if it passes host validation — the relation/schema registry for fact candidates, and domain conformance without unknown-to-covered conversion for Coverage — and anything failing that validation is refused before admission. The enumeration is demoted from 'named instances, not the trigger' to 'examples, not the trigger'.
repairAudit.assessment: This is the repair as specified, and it closes the seam exactly: NT-3's masquerading FactCandidate now fails the relation/schema registry limb, and NT-5's domain-mutating Coverage now fails the domain-conformance limb. Both are consequences of the rule rather than of the enumeration.

measured: negativeTests.wirePin gives path docs/coop/artifacts/delivery.v2.json and sha256 47b6cfd17338fafd407c554afe1951ab23d2896aac99bcfd272fc0894e3cabf3, which reproduces exactly from disk.

The note's claim that delivery.v4 is a derivation over v2 is true and stronger than stated: delivery.v3 AND delivery.v4 both declare derivedFrom delivery.v2.json at exactly the pinned digest 47b6cfd1, and delivery.v5 derives from v4.

The frame vocabulary lives only in v2's bytes. Counted in delivery.v2.json: HelloAck 7, UniverseAccepted 5, SnapshotAccepted 6, FactBatch 11, Unavailable 15, BudgetExhausted 13, Complete 15, Cancelled 9, FactCandidateV1 5, relationSchemaId 2. In v3, v4 and v5 those counts are zero except an incidental 'Complete' 2 in v4 — they are operation documents that do not restate the vocabulary. So v2 is the only bytes against which the classes can be constructed.

delivery.v4 measures applicationState 'NOT APPLIED', reviewState 'AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW', binds 'NOTHING'. The pinned base is therefore not merely a base but the operative document, which the artifact could have said and did not need to.
repairAudit.assessment: The pin is correct, resolvable, and survives the supersession attack I ran against it.

advisories.finding: The wirePin note reads 'DR-011-R04 contest on later checkers does not move this pin.' DR-011-R04's live text has two halves: 'reviewed v4 checker standing does not elevate later unreviewed check-delivery-v5.py' — the checker half the note names — and 'release fixtures remain inconsistent with the effective major-1 substrate', which the note does not mention and which is the half closer in subject to a wire pin.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: I tested the omitted half and it does not move the pin either. R04's fixture clause asserts that release fixtures fail to match the effective major-1 substrate; it does not impeach the substrate document, and this artifact's classes are specified against contract bytes rather than executed against fixtures, with status honestly 'specified-classes-not-executed'. The note's conclusion is therefore correct, and its route to that conclusion is merely incomplete. Recording the adjudication here so the corpus carries it either way.
advisories.suggestion: Widen the note to name both halves of R04 and say why neither moves the pin — the checker skew concerns instruments rather than the contract, and the fixture inconsistency measures fixtures against this very substrate rather than against the substrate's bytes. Adding that delivery.v4 measures NOT APPLIED / binds NOTHING would make the pin's standing self-evident.

advisories.finding: Carried unchanged from my v2 review: v1's identityDependencies block — routing Coverage sufficiency and subjectScopeCommitment to DR-006 / D-077, finding identity to D-077, and D9 values to DR-007 / D-078 — still has no successor. Measured in v3: identityDependencies, DR-006, D-077 and D-078 each occur zero times; DR-007 occurs twice, in typedNonSuccessOwner and NT-6.
advisories.whyNotBlocking: Nothing false is asserted in its place. NT-5's 'Sufficiency remains host-owned' is structural law preserved from V1 and file 01, and no statement in the artifact depends on a parked recipe. This was advisory at v2 and remains advisory.
advisories.suggestion: Restore the block in any successor. D-077 and D-078 are the dispositions the sibling row DR-131 is required to cite, and an artifact whose posture is honesty about what is parked reads stronger carrying the routing.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with 2 non-blocking advisories. Fifteen attacks run, two landed, both at advisory grade. Custody is intact: subject ef2a7416 at 0444 unmoved and valid JSON, predecessor v2 frozen at e91595a0, HEAD never left 52ea851, file 08, file 01 and COORD at their pins with a clean tree. Because v3 repairs my own three v2 findings, I tested each against live sources rather than my earlier text and ran a flattened-path diff to catch anything the repairs might have disturbed: 10 paths added, 7 changed, and zero removed, so every element carrying a v1-blocker repair is byte-identical to v2. SF1 is repaired — NT-6 restores the D9/exit class that had regressed and NT-7 adds planAdmission, and rebuilding the map from bytes shows 0 of 11 named prohibitions uncovered; NT-7 also reaches RequestId/ExecutionId allocation, which was not asked for. SF2 is repaired exactly as specified: the rule is now two limbs, type-level and content-level, with the content limb naming the relation/schema registry and Coverage domain conformance, so NT-3 and NT-5 are consequences of the rule rather than of the enumeration. SF3 is repaired, and I attacked the new pin rather than accepting it: delivery.v3 and v4 both declare derivedFrom delivery.v2.json at exactly the pinned digest 47b6cfd1, v5 derives from v4, the nine worker-to-host frame names and the FactCandidateV1 / relationSchemaId structures exist only in v2's bytes, and delivery.v4 measures NOT APPLIED with binds NOTHING — so the pin is on the operative base and survives the supersession attack. The v1 repairs re-verify independently: file 01's digest and closing sentence reproduce, and the may-return partition is still exactly 6 kept plus 1 removed against 7 live entries with no extras. The register cell quote and its three-fragment reconstruction are exact. Nothing invented, nothing SATISFIED, no implementation authorization. The two advisories are that the wirePin note names only one of DR-011-R04's two halves — I tested the omitted fixture half myself and it does not move the pin either, so the conclusion is right and only the summary is partial — and that v1's identityDependencies routing to DR-006, D-077 and D-078 is still absent, unchanged in grade from my v2 review. Neither blocks. This acceptance is of the artifact as an independently reviewed design-contract candidate only; it applies nothing, marks no row SATISFIED, opens no D-056 class, and executes no test.
